<reason>B wins by exposing the unsupported weighting at the center of A’s case: serious background psychiatric risks cannot simply be counted as harms prevented by treatment. A supplied a plausible mechanism, but insufficiently connected it to the claimed long-term net benefit. B also explained why low regret and monitoring do not capture or eliminate lasting harms. B answered pressure directly, while A repeatedly mischaracterized reasonable evidentiary requests as demands for certainty and substituted a precautionary argument for access for the proposition’s empirical comparison.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B capitalized on A’s acknowledgment that suicide reduction was only plausible: outcome severity must be weighted by how much treatment actually changes its probability. B then specified feasible longitudinal comparisons and transparent attrition analysis, directly undermining A’s accusation of an impossible evidentiary standard.</best_rebuttal>
